difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a commutative square of rings with a surjective base change, quasi-finiteness at a prime descends to the corresponding prime of the target (statement lines 30509-30524). The proof does not estimate fibre dimensions: it uses the product decomposition of the fibre at the given point provided by quasi-finiteness, transports that decomposition along the base change, and shows the point remains isolated in the new fibre by a dimension zero argument (proof lines 30526-30556). Carrying the decomposition through the surjection is the step that makes the isolation visible. H2.
